labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/1-causality
labels.notes: I printed Causal.notchedCausality. It sets le U := TransGen (notchedStep U) and lt U := TransGen (notchedChronalStep U). Every field of the library structure is discharged: Precausality (Causal/Causality.lean:55) plus le_of_lt, isOpen_lt_right and isOpen_lt_left (:77). notchedStep U a b means a <= b in the product order of R x R and segment R a b inside val '' U. notchedChronalStep asks both null coordinates to increase strictly. In null coordinates (u, v) = (t + x1, t - x1), the closed future cone is {du >= 0, dv >= 0} and the open one is {du > 0, dv > 0}. So I+(0) = Q = {u > 0 and v > 0}, and the carrier notchedPlane = {p.1 <= 0 or p.2 <= 0} is exactly R^{1+1} minus I+(0). It is closed (isClosed_notchedPlane). Its topology is the subtype topology of R x R, by mathlib's instance. It is a down-set of the product order, so a future causal segment that ends in M lies in M. That is what makes '<=_M is the product order on M' true. notchedCausality_le_top_iff proves it as an iff, and notchedCausality_lt_top_iff gives the strict form. I re-derived the openness of I+-_U(x). U is the trace of an open O of R^2 (isOpen_induced_iff). The last (or first) step's free endpoint moves within strict inequalities, and its segment stays in O by eventually_segment_subset_of_isOpen (Causal/OneWayMembraneChronal.lean:108). It stays in M by the down-set property. Nothing is degenerate. le is the product order on M, lt is nonempty (for example (-2,-2) << (-1,-1)), and only the edge points have an empty chronal future. The polygonal reading ('Minkowski's polygonal causality inside M', the target's title) is disclosed in the SCOPE, and causal arc-connectedness (label 2) makes it agree with the model's own curves.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/2-arc-connected
labels.notes: The theorem states Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected, the ladder's lean field (constants read off the elaborated type). A step is realised by the affine path into M, with the parameter clamped (notchedPath). Locally the path makes steps in any open N about its point: a convex ball, with the segment kept in M because it ends in M. Chains come from CurveOn.exists_concat. The lt half uses the same path, where both coordinates increase strictly. notchedCausality_absolutelyMinimal states Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal; the environment has no Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal, so the name resolves to the ladder's constant. notchedCausality_absolutelyMinimalOn W states Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn for every open W. Its #print says: for every cover S of W and every V <= W, each le_V and lt_V is a TransGen of relations in V inf O, O in S. That is the either-reading form of kb/0074 and OQ-18. The dual forms come from dual_causallyArcConnectedOn.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/3-push-up
labels.notes: notchedCausality_pushUp states Causal.Causality.PushUp (Properties.lean:69), which covers every open U, both signs, and both orders of composition. Lean reduces it with pushUp_iff. I re-derived both halves. For x << y <= z: I+_U(x) is open and contains y, so it contains y - (e, e). That point lies in M, because M is a down-set. The causal step from it to the next vertex is timelike, and lies in U for small e. Then induct along the chain. For x <= y << z: the first chronal step y -> d leaves room y + (m, m) <= d inside M. I-_U(z) is open, so it contains y + (e, e) for some e < m. The step x -> y + (e, e) is timelike, lies in M because it ends there, and lies in U for small e. Then head-induct. This replaces the sketch's tilted chains, and the REPORT says so.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/4-plain
labels.notes: notchedCausality_causallyPlain states Causal.Causality.CausallyPlain (Properties.lean:55). #print: for all U and all A, Int J+_U(A) is in cl I+_U(A) and Int J-_U(A) is in cl I-_U(A). That is defi:causalement_plat (ETT.tex:283-286), with A not even required to lie in U. The use of causallyPlain_of_locZ is legitimate. #check gives {S} : C.PushUp -> LocZplus C -> LocZminus C S -> interior S = empty -> C.CausallyPlain. There is no other hypothesis, and its axioms are standard. It is applied to C.dual with S = notchedEdge = M cap {u >= 0, v >= 0}, the two null half-lines bounding Q. C.dual.PushUp comes from dual_pushUp. LocZplus of C.dual asks for C-chronal past points in every neighbourhood: y - (e, e). LocZminus of C.dual off S asks for C-chronal future points: off the edge one null coordinate is negative, so y + (m, m) stays in M. interior_notchedEdge = empty holds in the subspace topology of M, which is the topology the lemma reads. Next to (0, v) lie (-d, v), and next to (u, 0) lie (u, -d). dual_causallyPlain (an iff) brings the result back to C. Nit: the docstring quote of the definition stops at the formula, with $$ written as $. It drops ', equivalently if every non-empty open subset of J^+-_U(A) meets I^+-_U(A)' and has no ellipsis. See the minor finding.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/5-causally-open-future
labels.notes: The theorem states Causal.Causality.CausallyOpenFuture: for all open U and V <= U, J+_U(V) is open. That is def:causally_open_spacetime_open as printed (ETT.tex:694-697), quoted verbatim apart from its first sentence. It is PushUp.causallyOpenFuture_of_chronalPastNeighbours applied to push-up and to ChronalPastNeighbours: every v in every open V has some p in V with p <<_V v, here v - (e, e). I checked it by hand near the edge. If (0, v) >= x with x in V, then x - (e, e) is in V and lies below every point of M within e of (0, v). The statement is not vacuous.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/6-not-causally-open
labels.notes: V is the open box (-1/2, 1/2) x (1/2, 3/2) about (0, 1), read in M. It lies on the notch's upper edge, it is the sup-norm ball of radius 1/2, and V cap M = V cap {u <= 0}. J-_M(V) contains the corner, by the null segment {0} x [0, 1], and lies in {u <= 0}: a point of V has v > 0, so u <= 0 because V lies in M. The points (e, 0) of M approach the corner, so J-_M(V) is not open (I re-derived this). The sketch used the ball about (0, -1/2); the closer uses the corner, which has the same mechanism and is disclosed. notchedCausality_not_causallyOpenPast states the negation of CausallyOpenFuture for notchedCausality.dual, which is definitionally 'J-_U(V) open for every U and V'. notchedCausality_not_causallyOpen negates Causal.Causality.CausallyOpen, two-sided by DEC-8, through its second conjunct.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/7-corner
labels.notes: notchedCausality_not_causallyOpenPastOn: no open W containing the corner has dual.CausallyOpenFutureOn W. The witnesses are U = W and V = W inf {v > 0}. J-_W(V) holds the corner, by a null segment to (0, d/2) inside a ball in W, and lies in {u <= 0}. Hence the theorem negates Causal.Causality.LocallyCausallyOpen, which #print shows to be LocallyCausallyOpenFuture C and LocallyCausallyOpenFuture C.dual. The second conjunct fails at the corner. This is stronger than the sketch's 'not locally causally open at the corner'. On chronal neighbours: nothing is <<_U after an edge point, because << would put the later point in Q. ChronalNeighbours is C.ChronalPastNeighbours and C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours (#print), and the second fails at the corner with V = top. On Tarentin (Properties.lean:116): it asks, for each x and each neighbourhood, p and q in it with x in openDiamond top p q. The corner lies in no open diamond at all. Indeed the corner has no chronal future, and the Lean proof shows that a top vertex above (e, 0) and (0, e) would lie in Q. Hence the space is not tarentin. That is stronger than 'not tarentin at the corner'. The cited ETT.tex:677-680 is def:tarentin_spacetime.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/8-ladder
labels.notes: Each result uses the ladder's constant. IsCausal holds because le lies in the product order. notchedCausality_diamond_eq gives diamond top p q = val^-1 Icc p q. It is compact by the closed embedding of the closed M (CausallyCompact), and GloballyHyperbolic is IsCausal plus compact diamonds (def:globally_hyperbolic, ETT.tex:995-996). StronglyCausalOpen (Properties.lean:109) takes an open V with p in V, V inside U, and CausallyConvexIn V top. The open sup-boxes of side 2d, read in M, are order-convex and every diamond lies in Icc, so they qualify. HasTimeFunction: u + v is continuous and strictly increases along le top between distinct points. StronglyCausal and CurvesExtend follow by causal_ladder. The time_function => curves_extend edge has standing T2 and second countable, and the subtype instances supply them.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/9-time-reversal
labels.notes: The dual is causally arc-connected, through dual_causallyArcConnectedOn. It is absolutely minimal, and AbsolutelyMinimalOn every W. Its time function is -(u + v). It is not LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, proved directly at the corner from not_causallyOpenPastOn. Plainness, push-up, GH and strong causality (open form) come through the library's dual_* iffs, whose types I read. dual 'causally open in the past' is C.CausallyOpenFuture, as the REPORT says. Not tarentin comes through dual_tarentin.

labels.label: T-abs-plain-not-open/10-separation
labels.notes: I read the constants off the elaborated types (getUsedConstants). notchedCausality_separates conjoins T2Space and SecondCountableTopology of the carrier with 18 ladder properties. It asserts 14 of them: AbsolutelyMinimal (Precausality), CausallyArcConnected, CausallyPlain, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, CausallyOpenFuture, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, IsCausal, CausallyCompact, GloballyHyperbolic, StronglyCausalOpen, StronglyCausal, HasTimeFunction and CurvesExtend. It negates 4: CausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpen, ChronalNeighbours and Tarentin. These are exactly the 18 causality-sort lean fields of programme/ladder.toml. notchedCausality_dual_separates asserts 12 for the dual and negates CausallyOpenFuture, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, CausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpen, ChronalNeighbours and Tarentin, again 18. The two _bare forms negate universal implications over Type-0 spaces with T2 and second countability. The first: AbsolutelyMinimalOn for every W (either reading), CausallyPlain, PushUp, GloballyHyperbolic and CausallyOpenFuture do not give LocallyCausallyOpen. The second: the same without CausallyOpenFuture does not give LocallyCausallyOpenFuture. One instance refutes each claim. The ladder edges are consistent. absolutely_minimal and causally_plain => push_up (T1) meets a model that is push-up. push_up and chronal_neighbours => causally_open meets a model that is not causally open and has no chronal neighbours, proved directly and re-derived backwards by causal_ladder. On the paper: causal plainness, even with absolute minimality (either reading), push-up, GH, strong causality and a time function, gives no causal openness, global or local. Future-only openness as printed fails for the dual, and DEC-8's two-sided form fails for both. That is accurate and not overstated. No ETT statement claims the contrary. Grepping ETT.tex for causalement_plat and plain gives :217, 283-286, 289-300, 304, 315-325, 478, 523-535, 554, 837-872, 955 and 1172, and none of them derives causal openness from plainness. prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal (:698-701) is consistent with both models: the notched plane fails two-sided openness and the local form, and the dual fails both future forms. The REPORT rightly records no paper finding.

findings.what: 'Two entries, one per orientation ... Neither orientation alone settles all four' is false. Re-simulated with the committed tools/ladder.py, the time reversal's entry alone (witness Causal.notchedCausality_dual_separates, to = causally_open_future) moves all four pairs, giving fails 268 -> 272 and open 28 -> 24. Its from contains causally_plain and absolutely_minimal. Lacking causally_open_future, it lacks causally_open, since causally_open => causally_open_future. Read backwards through absolutely_minimal and locally_causally_open_future => causally_open_future, it lacks locally_causally_open_future, hence locally_causally_open. So the notched plane's entry (to = causally_open) adds nothing to the matrix once the dual's is in: one entry is load-bearing, not two. The counts, the four removals, and the claim that the eight optional entries change nothing all stand. Recording both entries is harmless.
